title: Role Change Provenance and Audit Correlation Playbook
author: Samira Liu
body:
Summary:
This playbook describes the operational process and technical patterns we use at Redwood to capture, validate, and correlate role changes (entitlements, group membership, role delegations) with audit logs and evidence bundles required for compliance reviews and post-incident analysis. The document covers event taxonomy, minimum provenance data, storage/retention mapping, automated correlation recipes, manual triage procedures, and packaged evidence manifest examples.

Why this matters:
- Role changes are a primary signal in investigations about unauthorized access and privilege escalation.
- Audit logs without clear change provenance (who approved, which workflow, which commit/PR) are insufficient for regulatory evidence.
- Correlating change records and runtime access events reduces mean time to evidence (MTTE) and supports faster incident response and audit readiness.

Scope:
- Applies to all humans and service identities that can change RBAC state in Redwood-managed systems (IAM console, access-control service, SSO, Terraform-managed identity modules, and the internal admin UI).
- Does NOT replace role-approval policy text; it operationalizes evidence capture and correlation for changes that policy governs.

Key definitions and event taxonomy:
- RoleChangeEvent: an authoritative record emitted at the time a role or group membership is created, modified, or removed. Minimum fields: timestamp, subject (who changed), actor (who initiated), target (identity or group), before_state, after_state, change_id (UUID), approval_refs (zero-or-more), source (UI | API | IaC), origin_commit (optional), request_id.
- ApprovalArtifact: external proof that the change was authorized. Examples: PR id, approval ticket id, manager-approval signature from SSO, JIRA change-request ID.
- AccessEvent: runtime access attempt recorded by audit logging (e.g., access-granted, access-denied, impersonation, token-exchange).
- EvidenceBundle: a packaged set of RoleChangeEvents, ApprovalArtifacts, correlated AccessEvents, and packaging metadata used for audits or investigations.

Minimum provenance requirements (enforced at ingestion):
1) change_id (UUID) assigned on create and returned synchronously to mutating callers.
2) actor identity (id + auth_method) and IP.
3) source and request_id for cross-service correlation.
4) approval_refs captured when present; automated systems must attach PR/ticket references.
5) hash of before_state and after_state stored to detect tampering.

Event schema (example, represented for human readers):
| field | description | example |
|---|---|---|
| change_id | opaque UUID for the change | 8a2b7f5e-... |
| timestamp | RFC3339 timestamp | 2026-01-15T14:22:03Z |
| actor | identity id + method | user:alice@redwood (sso) |
| source | where change originated | admin-ui |
| request_id | trace id for correlation | req-0a12b3c4 |
| approval_refs | list of artifacts authorizing change | JIRA-4567, PR#234 |
| before_state | canonical JSON string of RBAC state pre-change | {...} |
| after_state | canonical JSON string of RBAC state post-change | {...} |
| integrity_hash | SHA256(before_state + after_state + change_id) | abc123... |

Storage and retention mapping:
- High-risk roles (SRE, Privileged-Admin, Billing-Admin): RoleChangeEvent retention = 10 years; audit logs retention = 7 years.
- Mid-risk roles (Team-Admin, Service-Deployer): RoleChangeEvent retention = 5 years; audit logs retention = 3 years.
- Low-risk roles (Read-only, Viewer): RoleChangeEvent retention = 2 years; audit logs retention = 1 year.
- Retention overrides must be approved by Legal and recorded in the Risk Exceptions register (see related_pages).

Correlation and evidence assembly recipes (automated):
- Recipe A: UI/API initiated change with approval refs
  1) Pull RoleChangeEvent by change_id.
  2) Expand approval_refs and fetch ApprovalArtifact content from ticketing/SCM APIs.
  3) Query access-audit-store for AccessEvents for subject identity in window [timestamp - 7d, timestamp + 7d].
  4) Validate integrity_hash and build EvidenceBundle: {change_event.json, approval_artifacts/, access_events.json, manifest.json} (manifest template below).
- Recipe B: IaC-initiated role change (Terraform apply)
  1) Capture origin_commit and pipeline_run_id and attach to change_event.
  2) Fetch pipeline audit logs, pipeline approver signatures, and PR review history.
  3) Correlate with runtime access events and include plan/apply diffs in the EvidenceBundle.

Manual triage runbook (use when automated correlation is incomplete):
1) Identify suspicious activity or audit request (owner: security oncall).
2) Run quick query: SELECT * FROM role_change_events WHERE target_identity = '<id>' ORDER BY timestamp DESC LIMIT 20; (examples below).
3) For each candidate change, fetch approval_refs and attempt to retrieve artifacts.
4) If approval artifacts unavailable, escalate to owner_team of source system for retention/hard-lookup.
5) If tampering suspected (integrity_hash mismatch), preserve storage snapshots (S3 object version, DB WAL segment) and open a forensic evidence job.

Evidence manifest template (manifest.json - included in every EvidenceBundle):
{
  "bundle_id": "bundle-<change_id>",
  "generated_by": "rbac-correlation-service v2.1",
  "generated_at": "<RFC3339>",
  "change_id": "<change_id>",
  "items": ["change_event.json", "approval_artifact-PR234.patch", "access_events.json"],
  "hash": "SHA256(...)",
  "retention_class": "high-risk",
  "owner_contact": "security@redwood.com"
}

Packaging and submission for audits:
- EvidenceBundle ZIP naming convention: redwood-evidence-<change_id>-<YYYYMMDD>.zip
- Bundles for regulatory audits must be staged in the compliance bucket (s3://redwood-compliance/<audit-id>/) with restricted ACL and an entry in the Evidence Registry (internal index).
- All bundles must include a checksum file and a chain-of-custody record (see packaging checklist).

Packaging checklist (for human or orchestration):
- [ ] change_event.json present and integrity-verified
- [ ] approval artifacts fetched and preserved (screenshot or full HTML/Text)
- [ ] access_events.json includes raw and normalized events
- [ ] manifest.json present and valid
- [ ] bundle checksum (SHA256) computed and recorded
- [ ] chain-of-custody metadata added (who assembled, who approved, timestamps)

Sample CLI queries and examples:
- Quick SQL (audit store):
  SELECT change_id, timestamp, actor, source, approval_refs FROM role_change_events WHERE target_identity = 'service:payments' AND timestamp > '2025-10-01' ORDER BY timestamp DESC;
- Example cURL to fetch a change event from the change-api:
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://internal-api.redwood/services/role-change/v1/events/<change_id>"
- Hash verification (Linux):
  cat change_event.json access_events.json | sha256sum - | awk '{print $1}'

Operational SLOs and KPIs:
- Evidence assembly time (EAT): 90% of EvidenceBundles generated within 60 minutes of request for changes classified as high-risk.
- Provenance completeness: >= 99.5% of RoleChangeEvents must include actor, request_id, and source.
- Approval artifact retrieval success: >= 95% for changes within the past 12 months (end-to-end fetch from ticketing/SCM).
- Tamper detection false-positive rate: < 0.1% (monitored weekly).

Automation and integrations recommended:
- Enrich the role-change ingestion pipeline to call the SCM and ticketing APIs when approval_refs are present, store artifact snapshots with the change_event (TTL aligned with retention policy).
- Add a server-side hook in IaC pipelines that writes origin_commit and pipeline_run_id into change events emitted by the IAM controller.
- Correlation microservice (rbac-correlation-service) should expose: /bundle?change_id=<id> and return a signed pre-signed URL to the staged ZIP in the compliance bucket.

Forensic preservation step-by-step (when tampering suspected):
1) Immediately set retention locks on the implicated S3 prefixes and DB tables (owner: infra-sre).
2) Snapshot underlying database (consistent backup) and isolate raw WAL segments.
3) Export raw audit log partitions for affected time window.
4) Create EvidenceBundle with additional forensic metadata and mark confidentiality=restricted.

Roles and ownership matrix:
- Security (owner): maintain playbook, run correlation service SLA, oncall for triage.
- Identity Platform (owner): ensure change_event schema enforced and synchronous change_id return.
- Infra-SRE: ensure audit log retention and snapshot tooling works for forensic preservation.
- Legal: approve retention exceptions and receive evidence packages for legal holds.
- Compliance Ops: package and submit EvidenceBundles for third-party audits.

Change controls and approval for playbook updates:
1) Draft changes in the security Git repo (docs/rbac-playbook).
2) Create RFC PR and tag reviewers (Security, Identity Platform, Infra-SRE, Legal).
3) After approvals, schedule a canary deployment of the rbac-correlation-service change and monitor EAT KPI for 72h.
4) Publish updated playbook page and notify compliance-ops.

Appendix A — Example correlation SQL snippets:
- Find access events around a change:
  SELECT * FROM access_events WHERE actor = '<actor_id>' AND timestamp BETWEEN TIMESTAMP_SUB('<change_ts>', INTERVAL 7 DAY) AND TIMESTAMP_ADD('<change_ts>', INTERVAL 7 DAY);
- Join access events with change events (simplified):
  SELECT c.change_id, c.timestamp AS change_ts, a.timestamp AS access_ts, a.action, a.resource FROM role_change_events c JOIN access_events a ON a.actor = c.target_identity WHERE c.change_id = '<change_id>' ORDER BY a.timestamp;

Appendix B — Examples of edge cases and recommended mitigations:
- Missing approval_refs for human-initiated UI changes: implement required fields on UI flows; default to blocking the mutation if approvals are required by policy.
- IaC changes where pipeline metadata is stripped: add enforcement in the pipeline agent to reject applies that do not sign change metadata.
- Long-tail storage cost for high-frequency low-risk changes: introduce rollup snapshots for viewer/read-only role churn and keep full details for attestable events only.

Contact and escalation:
- Primary owner: security@redwood.com (oncall rota: #sec-oncall)
- For evidence retrieval SLA breaches, escalate to: identity-platform@redwood.com and infra-sre@redwood.com
